Definition: luminousness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity; also a plant (as being bright)
BiblicalUsage: This word means both herb and light. In Kings a man went out to gather wild herbs for the pottage and found wild gourds, and in Esther the Jews had light and gladness and joy and honour when the king's decree was turned for their good.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the two meanings of this word belong together: the wild herbs that made the pottage bitter, and the light that shone on the Jews when they were delivered.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
